What it is for: The calm default: owns one horizontal lane at one of four heights. Allowed during Manta meetings.
Loops one side and leaves the way it came, handing the other half to the mediums. Allowed during meetings.
Sweeps a seat row; pushes the Octopus to the other seat row. Allowed during meetings.
Straight through the middle; splits the screen into top and bottom halves. Allowed during meetings.
Top to bottom through the center. Nothing crosses the middle while it is there; each half keeps its own fish.
Corner to corner; mediums take the two corners it leaves open.
A short fast lunge through the middle.
Circles one spot, then leaves the way it came. The only Hungry route allowed in meetings, on the far side.
Slow wavy pass through the lower middle: a long, easy target.
Drops in to look at one seat and climbs back out; that seat feels watched.
Lingers near the center with small turns.
Fast straight run across in 6-8 s: a jolt.
Fast zigzag; looks angry and is hard to track.
Fast corner-to-corner run.
Covers most of the screen. In a meeting no Shark lane fits, so the Shark waits off screen.
Straight glide in the top or bottom half; leaves the other half free.
Middle-to-low S; only the far edge is left for a meeting Shark.
Circles one side; followers bunch around it.
Glides along a seat row; that row gets the followers up close.
Corner to corner glide.
Patrols one seat row with a light weave. Also used for the pair patrol, mirrored on both rows.
Top row, then down a side.
Sways side to side along a row.
In and out on the same side.
Under the middle. Only when no Shark is on screen.
A short visit to one side.
Fast straight lane at one of five heights.
Corner to corner.
Dashes in, snaps back out the same side.
One hard angle.
Slow entry, then a fast exit.

Style: aims at a real Sardine or Anchovy school
What it is for: Cuts through a school, which scatters and regroups.
Corner to opposite corner as a block.
Two schools at once, mirrored, crossing in an X. Best used as the release right after a Shark leaves.
Corner to the neighbouring corner in an arch; flips to open up or down away from the Shark.
Stays on one side, corner to corner. The Tuna option while a Shark splits the screen.
Creeps in, holds still, then darts out to a corner.
Straight legs with a stop at every corner.
Darts in, stops, backs out the side it came from. Never crosses the middle.
Crawls along a seat row and rests twice.
Hops along the edge in bursts.
Comes up from under a seat, rests, sinks back.
Drops straight down (or up) through the screen.
Bounces off a seat row like a pool shot.
One long fast line.
A slow S through the center.
One lazy loop in the middle.
Dips to a seat and rests there.
Loops on one side. The Turtle option while a Shark splits the screen.
A lap around the whole table past every seat.
Corner to corner in an S.
Dips to the bottom seats three times.
A figure eight through the middle.
Along one seat row, around, back along the other.
Up from a bottom corner and across the top.
Slow diagonal, top-left to bottom-right.
Slow diagonal, bottom-left to top-right.
Steep drop from the top.
Straight down one side.
Drops in and hooks out the side.
Rises from the bottom and sinks back.
A long silver wave through the middle band. If: Use when the middle band is empty.

Rolls into a tight ball for 3 s, then streams away. A small crowd target. If: Not while a Shark lane is within 0.2 of the ball spot. Best right before a Marlin slash (gives it something to cut through).
Splits into two halves that go around the middle and meet again. If: Used when a Turtle or Puffer sits in the middle.
Follows 2 s behind a Marlin or Shark through its wake. If: Only after a fast big fish; keeps 2 s behind it, never ahead.
Swims to one seat, hangs there 3 s, and goes back the way it came. If: Target seat = the seat with the least tiny-fish time lately.
Hops along one seat row, a short stop at each seat. If: Alternate rows: top row, then bottom row next time.
Pops up from a seat edge, looks around, and dives back. If: Never under a Hammerhead rail patrol on the same row.
A slow flutter across the upper middle.
One loop in the middle, then on its way. If: No loop while the Manta is within 0.25.
Floats down from the top seats to the bottom seats. If: Pick a top seat with little traffic as the start.
Sharp zigzag across the screen.
Darts in, freezes for a second, then bolts.
Almost crosses, then turns back the way it came. If: Never toward a Shark lane.
A slow bobbing pass along the low middle.
Comes up from the bottom seats, turns, and sinks back. If: Mirror to the top half every other time so top seats get it too.
Stops in the middle for 4 s, an easy shared target. If: Not while a Shark is on screen.
Circles around a big fish while it travels (in game).
Drifts slowly with two stops to fan its fins.
Slides down a side edge, past the corner seats. If: Left and right edges take turns.
Climbs slowly from the bottom seats to the top seats. If: Pick the seat column with the least small-fish time.
Comes out of a corner, bobs up and down, goes back.
Two Seahorses, one from the top and one from the bottom, meet near the middle and go home. If: Only when the middle is clear of big fish.
Walks the full bottom row, past every bottom seat. If: Rows take turns: bottom, then top.
Walks toward the busiest spot, waits there 3 s, and walks back. If: Target = densest fish spot within 0.35 of a seat row.
Walks the top row upside down.
An S-wave right through the middle.
Follows the path of the biggest Sardine school so the chain hits. If: Only when a school of 6+ is on screen.
Runs the top row, snaps down through the middle, leaves along the bottom row.
Rises, draws a slow figure-8 in the middle, and sinks.
Drifts side to side, stopping at each seat column.
Two wide laps past every seat, then out.
Three straight passes: top, middle, bottom. Turns off screen. If: Order of rows is random each time.
Circles in, getting tighter, then breaks out.
Holds in the middle, leans toward the top seats, then the bottom seats.
Moves in short, fast jets with pauses between.
Rises up the middle and holds there a long time, then sinks. If: Tentacles sweep top row, then bottom row, during the hold.
Drifts across the lower half, very slowly.
Rises on the left, dives, and comes back up on the right.
